subject: Draft MAP: landing criteria, sprint signoffs, and acceptance tests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ellis <jamie@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP: landing criteria, sprint signoffs, and acceptance tests

Jamie — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a short mutual action plan focused on what "done" looks for the evaluation sprint so we can avoid last-minute scope/quality debates at handoff.

Attached: short MAP (PDF) and a first-pass acceptance test sheet. High level asks in the MAP:
- 3-week evaluation window (low-volume sandbox)
- Key success signals: 95% pass rate on intent extraction for core use cases, p95 latency < 350ms on sample dataset, no PII leakage in 2k sampled responses
- Acceptance gates at week 1 (smoke), week 2 (stability), week 3 (go/no-go)

Can you review and flag any must-have tests or procurement constraints from your side (Priya will be our compliance contact)? If this looks good we can lock the technical owner and timeline tomorrow.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: GL-MAP-proposal-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jamie Ellis <jamie@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@alliedmeds.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: landing criteria, sprint signoffs, and acceptance tests

Karthik — appreciate the quick turn. Overall this structure makes sense. A few notes from our side: 
1) We need a defined data retention demonstration for the sandbox (can't keep logs longer than 7 days).
2) Add a blue-team review for security on week 2 — Priya will coordinate.
3) We expect an initial model-concordance check against our in-house gold set (500 examples) before week 2.

I'll loop Priya into the thread. Can Marissa confirm the concordance test can run without redeploying our environment?

— Jamie
Head of Product, Greenline Health

On Wed, Jun 9, 2027 at 09:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jamie — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a short mutual action plan...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Jamie Ellis <jamie@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: landing criteria, sprint signoffs, and acceptance tests

Jamie / Karthik — quick technical confirmation from the infra side:
- Concordance test (500 examples) can run against a read-only snapshot of the sandbox. No redeploy required. We'll deliver a small runner and expected-report template.
- Data retention: we can configure ephemeral logs for the sandbox (7-day TTL) and provide hashed audit traces for the security review.
- Acceptance tests: I've added three measurable checks to the spreadsheet: false-positive rate threshold for entity extraction, average token-efficiency (tokens per successful extract), and a reproducibility check (stable outputs across 3 runs on same seed).

I attached the acceptance test sheet with the added rows. If these gates look right we'll schedule a short tech kickoff for Monday (30m).

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: technical-acceptance-tests.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Jamie Ellis <jamie@greenlinehealth.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@alliedmeds.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: landing criteria, sprint signoffs, and acceptance tests

Jamie / Priya — procurement/legal items to call out so they don't block the go/no-go: 
- Temporary sandbox NDA addendum (two-week clause) — can be executed by e-sign; I'll send a clean addendum today.
- Pricing: evaluation will be covered under the pilot credit schedule; we'll provide an invoice block only if production is requested during the eval.
- SLAs: evaluation is best-effort; any formal SLA will be part of the committed Dedicated quote.

If Greenline needs a longer retention proof-of-concept, we can scope that as a separate deliverable.

— Ben Carter
Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ellis <jamie@greenlinehealth.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@alliedmeds.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: landing criteria, sprint signoffs, and acceptance tests

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps: 
1) Action: Greenline to confirm the 500-example gold set delivery by Monday EOD (Jamie).
2) Action: Priya to schedule week-2 blue-team review (security).
3) Action: Marissa to run concordance test runner Friday of week 1 and publish report.
4) Action: Ben to send sandbox NDA addendum and credit confirmation.
5) Timeline: evaluation window 3 weeks starting Monday 2027-06-14; go/no-go decision 2027-07-05.

If no objections by EOD Monday I'll mark the MAP as final and update the shared doc with dates/owners. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
